hero.headline: Stuart downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation to expand slip capacity
hero.teaser: Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a year-long $3 million renovation that will expand capacity from 18 to 44 slips and add storm-resistant features.
hero.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation project expected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project, funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees, will nearly double the dock's capacity from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. More than 1,400 boaters use the dock annually.

Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, will continue running during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing the company to build a gate at the end of the non-floating section for passenger boarding. Boat captain Parker Fisher said the dock has needed work over the years and expressed hope that the project includes more floating docks. Kuyrkendall noted that Stuart's identity and economy are tied to the waterfront and acknowledged that busy weekends create crowding at the current dock.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, delivering a shrinking spending plan for the fourth consecutive year. The term-limited Governor exercised his veto pen to cut nearly $810 million in line-item vetoes, marking his final budget as Governor. DeSantis said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have, noting he was not trying to set a record after his historic $3.1 billion veto total in 2022.

The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. The spending plan sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades. However, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers' salaries. The Legislature had also proposed transferring an additional $750 million into the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new requirement from a proposed constitutional amendment passed by the House last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to reject 621 projects worth $830 million, which the group labeled budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 of those 621 appropriations. The Governor said he does not plan to be formally involved with any political committee to campaign for a proposed amendment after the Legislature changed his proposal, though he left open the possibility of participating if asked.

The budget takes effect as DeSantis approaches the end of his final term as Governor. He touted the spending plan as fiscally responsible while making strategic investments in infrastructure, education and environmental protection. The vetoed correctional officer salary increases and the decision to block the full rainy-day fund transfer represent two of the most significant cuts in the final budget package.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
cards.body:
A record-breaking number of Americans are hitting the roads this Fourth of July weekend, and South Florida drivers are contending with challenging conditions as a result. The AAA estimates that 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, with 61.4 million of those travelers choosing to drive. This marks an all-time high for car travel during the holiday. Friday's rainy weather created difficult driving conditions on the Florida Turnpike south of Orlando, testing drivers' patience and skills as they began their holiday journeys.

The wet weather made an immediate impact on travelers trying to navigate the crowded roads. One driver, Ed Budd, summarized the frustration many experienced, noting that conditions were beautiful until the rain arrived and drivers seemed to forget how to operate their vehicles safely. Despite these challenges, most travelers pushed forward with their plans. Driver Jim Macfawn, drawing on his years of experience on the road, said he simply adapts to whatever conditions come his way and keeps moving.

Orlando and Miami are among the top five travel destinations for Independence Day this year, according to AAA data. Driver experiences on the route between these two cities varied significantly. Carlos Borras and his wife completed their round trip between the two cities on Friday without incident, reporting smooth conditions with no traffic congestion or accidents along the way. However, driver Fernando Amado described a notably busier experience, attributing the heavy traffic to the rainy weather and noting that Friday appeared to be the day when most travelers were heading northward.

For those still planning to travel, AAA offers specific recommendations to help avoid the worst congestion. Travelers should consider departing after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday for the smoothest journey. The most severe traffic delays are expected between 10 a.m. and noon on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. AAA notes that the timing of travel, combined with your origin and destination, can significantly influence your overall road experience. As millions of Americans continue their holiday travels, checking weather forecasts and road conditions before departing remains essential for a safer journey.

cards.headline: Man fatally shot in parking dispute at South Florida Walmart
cards.teaser: A man was fatally shot during a parking dispute at a Walmart in South Florida.
cards.body:
A man was fatally shot in a parking dispute at a South Florida Walmart. The shooting occurred at the store on Saturday.

The fatal shooting stemmed from a dispute over parking. Video of the incident was reported.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities nationwide to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city honored this year.
cards.body:
The National Civic League announced Riviera Beach as one of 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award at its conference in Denver, making Riviera Beach the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the recognition reflects years of work focused on improving civic health and creating opportunities for residents to play a direct role in shaping the city's future. City leaders presented Riviera Beach as a first-time winner during the awards announcement.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership, and the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate. The city also cited the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of residents and that every event, project and challenge the city overcomes happens because the community shows up for one another. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher who was suspended last year after making social media comments abo.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Theobald's Facebook comments labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald's reinstatement, claiming that "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald gets his job back, with no timeline announced for a decision.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit is stationing two boats with medics in north and south Martin County as hundreds of boaters hit the water for the Fourth of July weekend.
cards.body:
Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby in north and south Martin County this Fourth of July weekend as hundreds of boaters take to the waterways. Lt. Brett Harry said the team expects heavy boat traffic throughout the holiday.

Boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, saying safety is their top priority on the water. Harry said his team will respond to emergencies ranging from stubbed toes to cardiac events and potential spinal injuries.

Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. He encouraged everyone to have fun and be safe on the water.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4 percent as inflation hits holiday meal prices
hero.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
hero.body:
The cost of celebrating Independence Day with a backyard cookout has increased significantly this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, representing a 4 percent increase from the previous year. The survey attributes this rise directly to inflation affecting grocery prices across multiple categories of food typically served at Fourth of July celebrations.

Several key ingredients for holiday meals have seen notable price jumps. Ground beef, a staple for hamburgers and hot dogs, is up 5.5 percent compared to last year. Hamburger buns have experienced an even steeper increase of 7.7 percent. Strawberries have been hit particularly hard, with prices climbing 12.4 percent due to damage from a Florida frost that affected the crop. Ice cream, another popular summer treat, has risen 5.3 percent in price. These increases across multiple items have combined to push overall cookout expenses higher for families planning their Independence Day celebrations.

Not all food prices have moved upward, offering some relief for budget-conscious shoppers. Potato prices have actually declined this year, providing savings for those planning to serve potato salads or potato chips. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades region can provide consumers with the best value for their money. These price decreases can help offset some of the increases seen in other categories.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends several strategies to manage cookout costs without sacrificing the celebration. She suggests comparing prices across different stores to identify which retailers offer the best deals on the items on your shopping list. Woroch emphasizes that reducing food waste represents the most significant way families can save money, and this process starts with developing a detailed meal plan before shopping. By planning meals in advance and shopping strategically, consumers can keep their Fourth of July cookout expenses under control despite the inflationary pressures affecting grocery prices this year.

cards.headline: Juno Beach residents seek fence replacement at JB-7 beach access as trespassing disputes mount
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer when people park on private spots and push through bushes with coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs. Hill said residents used to confront trespassers but now call police because people became rude. Without the fence, only bushes separate the public access path from private land.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring a lower-cost solution, proposing the town help with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs. Hill said residents are hoping the town will put the fence back up so they can have their landscaping and private parking. The council agreed to take up the fence question as part of its upcoming budget discussions on July 15. Beachgoer Michael House, who walks to JB-7 from a public lot a couple of blocks away, said he has never noticed anyone hopping the fence or shrubs.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby as Fourth of July boaters take to waterways
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters are expected on the water this Fourth of July weekend.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are heading to Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting maritime safety officials to prepare for increased holiday traffic. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team is expecting a surge in boaters and will have two boats with medics positioned in the north and south of Martin County on standby. "We're just out there to mitigate anybody that needs help, whether it's something as simple as a stubbed toe to anything cardiac related, or potential spinal injuries, or anything like that," Harry said.

Among those launching Friday at Sandsprit Park in Martin County were boaters Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who set out with their young daughter and puppy. The Shannons prioritize safety when hitting the water. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices before setting sail. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce property into artistic destination with global reach
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map while preserving the historic Crain Estate.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card Body

The Peacock House Art Foundation preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain at their historic Fort Pierce estate. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship appears throughout the facility on floors, walls, and ceilings. Art Director Krystal Masters said the estate remains 90 percent unchanged from when the Crains lived there, as the foundation has consciously preserved the original character without commercializing it. The property includes distinctive spaces like a smoking and bourbon room with wood paneling and stained glass that opens onto a front patio bar.

The Crains collected items during nine world trips, including a gazebo shipped from India that features peacock designs. Guided tours of the gardens and architecture are available Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The estate's name comes from peacocks the Crains introduced to Fort Pierce in the 1970s. Starting with seven birds, the population has grown to over 100, including Bob, believed to be 60 years old, who walks with a limp and is hand-fed daily. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts international artists with on-property accommodations, while the art lab offers classes in sculpting, watercolor, and other mediums for children and adults of all skill levels.

cards.headline: Delray Beach's S.D. Spady Elementary jumps from C to A rating as Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County earned an A rating from the state for the third consecutive year, with S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach making a dramatic leap from a C rating to an A.
cards.body:
Principal Rona Tata, who has served 15 years as principal and five years as assistant principal before that, led the turnaround at S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach. The school earned an A rating this year after receiving a C rating the previous year. Tata said the school had an A rating two years ago and narrowly missed a B rating last year by just a few points. Three years ago, staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels, contributing to the renewed A rating. The school fine-tuned its entire academic approach, focusing on testing grades while also challenging students and staff to raise expectations across campus. The school's theme last year was "Be the reason you succeed."

Community member Chris Ceasar, who attended Spady as a child and now has family members enrolled there, said the A rating will draw more talent to the school and allow students being bused to other schools to return to their community. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a C rating to an A this year, alongside Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary. District-wide, 143 district-operated schools, or 84 percent, earned A or B ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district also achieved a record-setting 93.5 percent graduation rate.

According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, representing a 4% increase from the previous year. The price hike reflects broader inflationary pressures affecting groceries across the board, making it more challenging for households to maintain their summer grilling traditions without stretching their budgets.

The survey reveals which foods are driving up costs. Ground beef prices have increased 5.5%, while bun prices jumped 7.7%. Strawberries have been hit particularly hard by a Florida frost, climbing 12.4% in price. Ice cream, a popular summer dessert staple, is up 5.3%. These increases in key cookout ingredients mean that traditional Fourth of July menus will require more careful planning and shopping than in previous years.

However, not all food prices have increased. Potato prices have dropped this year, providing some relief for families planning to serve potato chips or potato salad at their gatherings. cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves land transfer for new Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to FDOT to assist with a partial interchange coming to Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County.
cards.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike at Midway Road. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the city currently has a significant gap between Turnpike entrances and exits. The interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

The $95 million Midway Road Widening Project is underway to address congestion and safety. Crews are currently in the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding the partial interchange, which is still in the design phase. The project will include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. The city council will vote on final approval of the land transfer at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Glydways proposes elevated autonomous transit from West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: A California-based autonomous transit company is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles that would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present its proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport, the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations using small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers along a dedicated elevated guideway. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the concept functions like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without traffic delays or intermediate stops. Estimated travel times would be seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center. Gettinger noted that West Palm Beach is uniquely positioned because major transportation hubs already exist close together but lack easy pedestrian or traveler connections, with increasing congestion along Okeechobee Boulevard, Southern Boulevard and Belvedere Road.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of traditional light rail, which carries South Florida estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile, while offering comparable passenger capacity. Potential funding sources include Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Gettinger emphasized the service would be priced like public transit, not private rideshare. The company said the technology is safer than self-driving cars because vehicles run on a fully dedicated guideway separated from traffic and rail crossings. Tuesday's meeting would determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal rather than approve construction.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation draws global artists to Fort Pierce historic estate
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, putting the Peacock Arts District on the map and connecting local and international artists.
cards.body:
Tucked away in the historic Crain Estate, the Peacock House Art Foundation is a non-profit organization preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once owned the property. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Many parts of the house remain largely unchanged from the Crains' time there, including the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling, manly-colored bathroom, and prestained glass leading out to the front patio bar. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, starting with seven birds that have since grown to over 100. Among the flock is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and known for walking with a limp. Bob lives in the estate and is hand-fed daily from his own bowls.

The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations on the property. No professional experience is required to participate. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with Krystal Masters, the art director, leading one-on-one classes designed for complete beginners. Students come in with zero experience and leave with a finished piece of art.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue two boaters after vessel sinks in Intracoastal
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, thanks to a quick response from marine deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit responded to reports of a small motorized boat taking on water and becoming submerged on July 1. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Both occupants ended up in the water when their boat went down, but deputies say they were wearing life jackets that kept them afloat while help arrived. Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

The Martin County School Board is fighting back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended last year over social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, claiming "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney characterized Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, which labeled him as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, as a "serious offense" and said removing him was appropriate.

Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling in her order, noting that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds on personal equipment with no student involvement violated First Amendment rights. She recommended Theobald receive back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but stated they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority over whether Theobald returns to his position, with no decision date announced.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman remembered after deadly home fire Monday
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a Hobe Sound home fire that preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiancé, Mark, rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, said she learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. Fenn described the scene as "completely a state of devastation." She remembered White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, and playing piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand," Fenn said. "She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people." The loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his son, Jacob. White's birthday was July 4, just days after her death on Monday.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of 10 communities nationwide to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, recognizing efforts to strengthen community engagement.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach is celebrating being named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. Riviera Beach was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment. These include the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating that the award belongs to the entire community. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between June 27 and July 5, with 61.4 million making the trip by car.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with AAA estimating 72.2 million people will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Heavy rain on Friday created difficult driving conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd said conditions were beautiful until the rain started and everyone forgot how to drive. Despite the challenging weather, driver Jim Macfawn said he has a lot of experience driving and just rolls with the punches. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA.

Experiences on South Florida roads varied widely on Friday. Carlos Borras and his wife made the round trip between Orlando and Miami and reported smooth sailing with no traffic or accidents. Driver Fernando Amado described a very different experience, saying it has been pretty busy, especially with the weather. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are targeting a state title in the 2026 fall football season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. Despite the successful regular season, a second-round playoff exit has motivated the program to aim higher. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson noted that the senior class is uniquely positioned to lead this push, with most of them being four-year players who came through the middle school program. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

To compete at a higher level, Saint Andrew's has intentionally scheduled more challenging opponents for the fall. Senior Jack Williams emphasized the program's commitment to elevating its performance, stating that playing against strong teams will help attract new talent. For the Scots, improvement this season is measured primarily by postseason advancement. Senior Jack Whelche explained that while going undefeated in the regular season would be ideal, the true measure of success is advancing further in the playoffs. The team is using summer workouts as motivation for the season ahead, with senior Edmyer St. Jean highlighting how daily training builds anticipation for results.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs through September during peak sea turtle nesting season. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups are encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and America 250 events

Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County. The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: Florida offers free state park admission through Sunday for America's 250th birthday
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection is waiving admission fees at state parks through July 5 to celebrate America's semiquincentennial.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection is waiving admission fees to state parks from Friday, July 3, 2026, through Sunday, July 5, 2026, to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. DEP Secretary Alexis A. invited all Floridians, their friends and family to explore the state's parks during this significant moment in the nation's history. Florida's award-winning state parks offer hiking, camping, wildlife viewing, swimming, paddling and horseback riding alongside historic sites including forts, battlefields, archaeological sites and landmarks. The Florida State Park system is the only four-time winner of the NRPA's National Gold Medal Award.

Free admission applies to day use only at most locations. Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park, Skyway Fishing Pier State Park and Weeki Wachee Springs State Park are excluded from the promotion. All other fees, including overnight accommodations, special events, concessions and rentals, remain in effect. Over the last fiscal year, Florida State Parks welcomed more than 28 million visitors and generated an estimated $3.6 billion in statewide economic impact. Visitors can plan trips at FloridaStateParks.org.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, delivering a shrinking spending plan for the fourth consecutive year. The term-limited Governor exercised his veto pen to cut nearly $810 million in line-item vetoes, marking his final budget as Governor. DeSantis said he vetoed items he considered either inappropriate or nice to have, noting he was not trying to set a record after his historic $3.1 billion veto total in 2022.

The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. The spending plan sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades. However, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers' salaries. The Legislature had also proposed transferring an additional $750 million into the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new requirement from a proposed constitutional amendment passed by the House last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to reject 621 projects worth $830 million, which the group labeled budget turkeys. DeSantis ultimately vetoed 184 of those 621 appropriations. The Governor said he does not plan to be formally involved with any political committee to campaign for a proposed amendment after the Legislature changed his proposal, though he left open the possibility of participating if asked.

The budget takes effect as DeSantis approaches the end of his final term as Governor. He touted the spending plan as fiscally responsible while making strategic investments in infrastructure, education and environmental protection. The vetoed correctional officer salary increases and the decision to block the full rainy-day fund transfer represent two of the most significant cuts in the final budget package.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida communities stage fireworks, parades and drone shows for semiquincentennial
cards.teaser: Fourth of July weekend brings celebrations across Southwest Florida marking America's 250th birthday, with events planned from Sarasota to Fort Myers Beach.
cards.body:
Communities across Southwest Florida are hosting fireworks, parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations for Independence Day weekend as the nation marks its 250th birthday. Events are planned from Sarasota's bayfront and Nathan Benderson Park to Manatee County, Venice, North Port and Fort Myers Beach.

Bradenton and Palmetto will celebrate together with festivities on both sides of the Manatee River, including activities along the Bradenton Riverwalk, Rossi Park, Old Main Street and Palmetto's Riverside Park. Palmetto's 15th annual Fourth Fest at Riverside Park will feature 14 food trucks, 20 artisan and community vendors, a kids zone and live music, with fireworks visible from both sides of the river. Sarasota's bayfront will host the city co-sponsored America250 fireworks display beginning at 9 p.m. Waterside Place in Lakewood Ranch will celebrate with circus acts, carnival games, a kids zone, food and a drone show over the water at 9 p.m. Siesta Beach will host its 35th annual community fireworks show from 8 to 9:30 p.m., with the display 100% funded by local residents, businesses and community supporters. Fort Myers Beach will kick off celebrations with a parade starting at 10 a.m. at Bay Oaks Recreation Center, heading down Estero Boulevard to Times Square, followed by fireworks launched from a barge near Times Square around 9 p.m., with Matanzas Pass Bridge closing from around 8:30 to 11:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Marion County stages four synchronized fireworks displays for America's 250th
cards.teaser: Ocala and Marion County are celebrating the semiquincentennial with four simultaneous fireworks shows and community events under the Marion Celebrates 250 banner.
cards.body:
Marion County will stage synchronized fireworks displays at four locations on July 4, each beginning at 5 p.m. with live entertainment, food vendors and family activities before fireworks at 9 p.m. The sites are Veterans Memorial Park in Ocala, Wrigley Fields in Citra, Dunnellon High School in Dunnellon and the Belleview Sportsplex in Belleview. The celebrations mark the semiquincentennial, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

Before the evening fireworks, the city of Ocala is hosting Fourth in the Park at Tuscawilla Park starting at 10 a.m., a free celebration with live music, food trucks, a kids zone and games. Country singer-songwriter Emma Forgette performs from 10 to 11:30 a.m., followed by Nashville recording artist Cliff Dorsey from noon to 2 p.m. The city is also opening its aquatic fun centers, splash pads and the Discovery Center for free patriotic pool parties and activities. The Patriot Parade will kick off at Southeast 16th Avenue, head up to Silver Springs Boulevard and wrap up near Southeast 25th Avenue, with veteran groups, local businesses and community organizations marching in the early evening.

cards.body:
Historic Downtown Venice will celebrate America250 and the city's centennial with a patriotic parade through the city beginning at 9:30 a.m. at West Venice Avenue and Avenue des Parques, ending near West Blalock Park. The event marks both the nation's semiquincentennial and Venice's 100th anniversary.

Venice's America250 fireworks show will be held in the evening at the South Jetty, scheduled to start between 9 and 9:15 p.m. Officials already announced contingency plans to reschedule to July 5 in case of inclement weather. The dual celebration reflects the city's commitment to marking both national and local milestones during the Independence Day weekend.

cards.body:

hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida roads
hero.body:
A record-breaking number of Americans are hitting the roads this Fourth of July weekend, and South Florida drivers are contending with challenging conditions as a result. The AAA estimates that 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, with 61.4 million of those travelers choosing to drive. This marks an all-time high for car travel during the holiday. Friday's rainy weather created difficult driving conditions on the Florida Turnpike south of Orlando, testing drivers' patience and skills as they began their holiday journeys.

The wet weather made an immediate impact on travelers trying to navigate the crowded roads. One driver, Ed Budd, summarized the frustration many experienced, noting that conditions were beautiful until the rain arrived and drivers seemed to forget how to operate their vehicles safely. Despite these challenges, most travelers pushed forward with their plans. Driver Jim Macfawn, drawing on his years of experience on the road, said he simply adapts to whatever conditions come his way and keeps moving.

Orlando and Miami are among the top five travel destinations for Independence Day this year, according to AAA data. Driver experiences on the route between these two cities varied significantly. Carlos Borras and his wife completed their round trip between the two cities on Friday without incident, reporting smooth conditions with no traffic congestion or accidents along the way. However, driver Fernando Amado described a notably busier experience, attributing the heavy traffic to the rainy weather and noting that Friday appeared to be the day when most travelers were heading northward.

For those still planning to travel, AAA offers specific recommendations to help avoid the worst congestion. Travelers should consider departing after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday for the smoothest journey. The most severe traffic delays are expected between 10 a.m. and noon on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. AAA notes that the timing of travel, combined with your origin and destination, can significantly influence your overall road experience. As millions of Americans continue their holiday travels, checking weather forecasts and road conditions before departing remains essential for a safer journey.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce waterfront hosts 16th annual boat parade
hero.teaser: The Fort Pierce waterfront turned red, white and blue on Saturday for the 16th annual boat parade celebrating Independence Day.
hero.body:
Fort Pierce residents and visitors gathered along the waterfront Saturday to celebrate Independence Day during the community's 16th annual boat parade. Decorated in patriotic red, white, and blue, the boats created a festive atmosphere as the parade marked another year of this cherished Fourth of July tradition on the Fort Pierce waterfront. The event has grown into a signature celebration for the area, drawing both longtime residents and visitors who want to be part of the holiday festivities.

The boat parade represents one of several ways the Fort Pierce community comes together to celebrate and connect. The waterfront serves as a gathering place for residents throughout the year, hosting various events and activities that bring people together. Saturday's parade continued a tradition that has become an important part of Fort Pierce's cultural calendar, allowing the community to share in the patriotic spirit of Independence Day on the water.

Beyond the boat parade, Fort Pierce offers visitors and residents other attractions and cultural experiences. The Peacock House Art Foundation has emerged as a significant destination, transforming the area into an artistic hub. The foundation preserves the historic Crain Estate, a property that reflects decades of history and craftsmanship. According to Krystal Masters, the art director, the estate was once home to Jaxson and Mary Crain, whose dedication to artistry is evident throughout the facility. Mr. Crain's work as a tile craftsman is visible in detailed tilework that spans from the ground to the walls and ceiling.

The estate remains largely unchanged from the Crains' era, maintaining approximately 90 percent of its original character. The couple traveled the world nine times and collected unique pieces for their Florida home, including a gazebo shipped from India. The property is also known for its peacocks, which have roamed the grounds for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced the birds to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, beginning with seven peacocks that have since grown to over 100. Among the flock is Bob, believed to be the oldest peacock on the property at around 60 years old. Visitors can take guided tours of the Peacock House's lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, experiencing the blend of history and artistry that defines this Fort Pierce landmark.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation preserves historic Crain Estate and attracts international artists to Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate and connecting local and inter.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination by preserving the historic Crain Estate and connecting local and international artists. The non-profit operates from the former residence of Jaxson and Mary Crain, offering guided tours every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker whose craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items including a gazebo shipped from India that features tiny peacocks. The foundation has maintained 90 percent of the estate as it was when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room with its man paneling and stained glass.

The Peacock House gets its name from the birds the Crains are believed to have introduced to Fort Pierce in the 1970s. They originally brought in seven peacocks, which have grown to over 100. Among the flock is Bob, believed to be 60 years old and recognizable by his limp. Bob lives in his own area with personal bowls and receives hand-feeding daily. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world and offers simple but elegant accommodations. Art director Krystal Masters leads the art lab, which offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, including one-on-one instruction in mediums such as sculpting and watercolor for complete beginners.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year
cards.teaser: A holiday cookout meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July cookout tradition comes with a higher price tag this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased costs. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%.

Not all items have increased in price. Potato prices are down this year, which benefits potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping more strategically by comparing stores to find the best deals for items on your grocery list. She emphasized that the biggest way families can manage costs is by cutting down food waste, which begins with creating a meal plan.

cards.teaser: A condominium at 2636 Ocean Drive Apt 506 in Vero Beach is now listed for sale.

cards.headline: FSU Baseball lands commitment from FGCU pitcher Sebastian Lippman
cards.teaser: Florida State University's baseball program earned a commitment from Florida Gulf Coast University right-handed pitcher Sebastian Lippman.
cards.body:
The Florida State Seminoles baseball team gained a commitment Saturday from FGCU right-handed pitcher Sebastian Lippman. The announcement came July 4 as the Seminoles continue to build their roster.

Lippman pitched for Florida Gulf Coast University before committing to FSU. The right-handed pitcher will join the Seminoles baseball program after his time at FGCU.
